title: The S9 context pack and the S9 module extracts are absent from the workspace
source: WP B2-S9-017 read-only list (_work/msr/context/S9.md and _work/msr/extract/ files whose name contains S9, module Partner); knowledge of the workspace root
description: The work package names a context pack and a set of module extracts as the authority for service facts, the ownership rows and the naming rules, and neither the context folder nor the extract folder exists in this workspace. The service row, the ownership rows of partner, partner_user, partner_instruction, recovery_case and decision_log_entry, and the slide references are therefore taken from Template and Rules v1 R4, the S9 story set of this folder and the primary slice RWB-P5-E1032-APP, which state the naming rule and the table owners but not the slide-level call types.
evidence: _work/msr holds only assumptions, editlog, fragments, gaps and smoke; the same absence is recorded by the earlier work packages B2-S2-015 and B2-S8-008 as CG-B2-S8-008-1
proposed: Issue the S9 context pack with the service row, the six ownership rows and the connection matrix row, and re-check sections 1, 3 and 12 against it; the naming, the ownership and the boundaries already agree with Template and Rules R4

title: No source states the partner boundary of the E1-032 split
source: legacy RWB-E1-032 sections 2 and 19; FSD P5 A2.12; the primary slice RWB-P5-E1032-APP; WP B2-S9-017 story line (secondary true, acs empty)
description: The legacy story names partner files as one of the three sources that arrive without a case link, and it owns the match, the store and the reviewer path inside the document hub; it says nothing about a partner-service duty, and RWB-E1-057 owns the partner SFTP intake of the document hub. The work package marks this story secondary and gives it no legacy AC, so the boundary between the document-hub slice and the partner slice is fixed by this story: the partner service owns the submission row, the partner reference of the case, the acceptance record and the attach state, and it owns no document, no intake item, no match and no resolution.
evidence: legacy RWB-E1-032 section 2 sentence on partner files; section 19 out of scope; WP B2-S9-017 line for RWB-S9-E1032-APP: secondary true, acs empty, TCs of the legacy key
proposed: Confirm the split at the wave 1 baseline review: if the partner service is to keep the file or to match the case itself, this story gains a store and a matcher and the P5 slice loses them; until then the boundary of section 1 and section 19 stands and no value is invented

title: The story wave and the service wave of rwb-partner disagree
source: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.6; Arch v5 service table (S9 rwb-partner, wave 4); WP B2-S9-017 story line (wave 1, EP01)
description: The business epic EP01 maps to wave 1 in the W-MAP while Arch v5 puts rwb-partner in wave 4, so the story carries the earlier W-MAP wave and releases on the Epic 1 date although the service is a wave 4 service. R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave and asks for one conflict gap per service and business epic; no source states how a wave 1 story of a wave 4 service is sequenced against the wave 4 platform work.
evidence: Template and Rules R4 service table row S9 wave 4; R5.6 W-MAP row EP01 wave 1; WP B2-S9-017 metadata line for wave and release
proposed: Keep wave 1 and the 30 November 2026 release as the work package fixes them, and state in the delivery plan that the partner channel of the intake ships with Epic 1 while the rest of rwb-partner follows in wave 4; no date is changed

title: The H row is empty and the C row is narrow while the DP table adds seven platform baselines and two contracts
source: WP B2-S9-017 story line (H empty, C RWB-P5-E1032-CON); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R5.7
description: The fixed pattern set adds seven H rows in R5.5 (DP-03 E1027, DP-06 E1042, DP-07 E1043, DP-09 TE006, DP-10 E1071, DP-15 E1044, DP-19 N001) and two C rows (DP-06 RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-07 RWB-P3-E1043-CON), while the work package fixes H empty and the C row at the document-hub contract only. The metadata copies the work package, and section 13 states that the platform rows arrive with the service template and the two list contracts with the client library, so they block no build.
evidence: WP B2-S9-017 line for RWB-S9-E1032-APP: H [], C [RWB-P5-E1032-CON], patterns DP01, DP03, DP05, DP06, DP07, DP09, DP10, DP11, DP15, DP19; Template and Rules R5.5 rows DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15, DP-19
proposed: Record the seven platform CON rows and the two list contracts on this key in the next plan issue, or state once in the plan that a platform CON is a shared Day-1 baseline and adds no per-story H row; this story keeps the fixed rows

title: No contract story publishes the partner document operations, the event or the intake creation
source: WP B2-S9-017 story line (C row names RWB-P5-E1032-CON only); RWB-P5-E1032-CON operations; TSD S9 API rows for the instruction
description: The partner submission operation, the submission read, the event name and its catalogue ID and the activity names are published by no source: TSD S9 lists the instruction, panel and scorecard operations, and the contract row of the work package names the document-hub baseline only. The document-hub intake creation that a partner file needs lies outside the four operations RWB-P5-E1032-CON publishes (resolve, list, item read, content read), so its path and shape are unpublished too.
evidence: RWB-P5-E1032-CON 12.1 in RWB-P5-E1032-APP: four operations and no creation; WP B2-S9-017 C row; no S9 CON story exists for the legacy key
proposed: Publish the two partner operations, the event and the intake creation in the S9 contract baseline and in the document-hub baseline before the wave 1 release, and give the event its catalogue ID; this story fixes the paths as its design choice until then

title: The acceptance decision code, the intake bound and the parameter row are not specified
source: legacy RWB-E1-032 sections 3 and 13; FSD P5 A2.12; TSD S9; RWB-P5-E1032-APP section 13
description: The legacy story fixes three parameters in the document-hub table (the case number pattern, the account number pattern and the classification threshold) and leaves the decision code open; it states no file size or body bound and no parameter row of the partner service. The partner acceptance therefore needs a decision code, a version in force and an intake bound that no source names, while the document types and the match states it uses are the legacy values.
evidence: legacy RWB-E1-032 section 3 parameters and section 13 build steps; no partner parameter row in any S9 table; RWB-P5-E1032-APP 13 keeps the three parameters in document_hub_parameter
proposed: Load the decision code of the acceptance and the intake bound as reference and parameter rows with the data steward, and name the parameter row of this service; the story reads both at their version and types neither in code

title: No data model carries a partner-side intake row
source: Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary (partner, partner_user, partner_instruction only); TSD S9 T3.1; legacy RWB-E1-032 sections 11 and 13
description: The partner service owns three business tables and none of them can hold a file submission, its hash, its intake item or its state, and no source states whether the partner service keeps a submission row at all. The story creates partner_intake in rwb_partner with the columns of section 11 and no field ID, because the data model carries none.
evidence: S9 tables of this story folder: partner (DF-PRT-001 to 007), partner_instruction (DF-PRT-008 to 016), partner_user (DF-REF-212 to 217); no document or intake table in the S9 ownership rows
proposed: Add partner_intake to the LDM with field IDs in the next issue and confirm that the partner service keeps no file; until then the table and its columns are this story's design content

title: The plan lists the seventeen legacy test cases on a story with no legacy AC
source: WP B2-S9-017 story line (acs empty, tcs_legacy lists TC-E1-032-01 to TC-E1-032-17); Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s7 and s16
description: The work package gives this story an empty acceptance-criteria list and the full legacy test-case list, while R7.2 asks each story to keep the test cases of the criteria it owns. The legacy criteria and their test cases are owned by the primary slice RWB-P5-E1032-APP, so this story carries seven new criteria and eight new test cases and executes no legacy test case; the legacy identifiers are named once in section 16 so that no test loses its trace.
evidence: WP B2-S9-017 line: acs [], tcs_legacy seventeen identifiers, secondary true; Template and Rules R7.2 s16; RWB-P5-E1032-APP sections 7 and 16
proposed: Either record the legacy test cases against the primary slice in the plan or state the rule for a secondary slice; the Test Cases master keeps one row per test and no test is duplicated

title: The partner portal screen of a document submission is not numbered
source: FSD S9 screens PRT-01 to PRT-04; legacy RWB-E1-032 section 15 (SCR-30 and SCR-31 belong to the document hub)
description: The legacy screens of the story are the document-hub review queue and the case documents, and the partner portal screens of S9 are numbered PRT-01 to PRT-04 without a document tab in any source. The screen on which a partner submits a file against an instruction is therefore one of them and which one is not stated.
evidence: FSD S9 screen list PRT-01 to PRT-04; legacy RWB-E1-032 section 15; the S9 story set of this folder uses SCR-34, SCR-35 and SCR-36 for staff
proposed: Name the portal screen of the document submission in the next FSD issue and add the field list to the platform edge story; the story keeps the placeholder until then
